current_text.html: To preserve the purity of the preaching of the Gospel, no man is permitted to preach in the pulpits of the Presbyterian Church in America on a regular basis without proper licensure from the Presbytery having jurisdiction where he will preach. An ordained teaching elder who is a member in good standing of another Presbytery of the Presbyterian Church in America may be licensed after being examined as to his views, according to the provision of BCO 13-6. This license shall immediately become void if the minister's own Presbytery administers against him a censure of suspension from office or the sacraments, or deposition from office, or of excommunication (in the event of such censures, the Presbytery with jurisdiction shall always notify the licensing Presbytery). A ruling elder, a candidate for the ministry, a minister from some other denomination, or some other man may be licensed for the purpose of regularly providing the preaching of the Word upon his giving satisfaction to the Presbytery of his gifts and passing the licensure examination. (See also BCO 22-5 and 22-6.)

relationships.title: Who May Be Licensed to Preach the Gospel

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB stated that a man not a ruling or teaching elder and not pursuing eldership may nonetheless be licensed to preach per the plain wording of BCO 19-1.

relationships.title: Minister from another denomination serving as stated supply

occurrences.excerpt: A minister from another denomination licensed by a PCA presbytery may serve as stated supply but may not administer sacraments unless his denomination has fraternal relations with the PCA or his sacramental views are consistent with PCA standards.

relationships.title: Prohibition of dual candidacy under BCO 18-7

occurrences.excerpt: BCO 18-7 permits a candidate to retain home-church membership while under another presbytery's care, but does not allow simultaneous candidacy under two presbyteries.

relationships.title: BCO 40-5 Matter re Metropolitan NY

occurrences.excerpt: Furthermore, it is the position of Metropolitan New York Presbytery that it is permissible for unordained and unlicensed men to occasionally preach (BCO 19-1), but not a woman.

metadata.synopsis: A BCO 40-5 citation arose from Metro New York Presbytery's failure to redress a session that allowed a woman to expound Scripture in place of the sermon preceding the Lord's Supper, held services without preaching, and celebrated the Supper without a preceding sermon. The SJC remitted the matter to the presbytery for constitutional resolution because the session's later no-exception response was clearly inadequate and the unapproved minutes were unclear. Presbytery must complete its work with TE Higgins and Trinity Presbyterian Church's session and report to the 51st General Assembly. A separate procedural note questioned the Assembly's direct referral but did not void it.

relationships.title: Troxell v. Presbytery of the Southwest

metadata.synopsis: A complaint challenged Presbytery’s institution of two charges against a teaching elder and related pretrial actions. The SJC annulled the household-management charge because process began fifteen months after the alleged offense and the record showed no recently flagrant, newly evident, or continuing offense under BCO 32-20. It also held that declaring the elder not in good standing removed rights without process, but left his properly imposed suspension effective. It rejected objections to discussion, questioning, and the timely submission charge, which could proceed without any determination of guilt.

relationships.title: Antioch Session v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: 2. Did ECP err in allowing Mr. Peterson to serve as Stated Supply for at least six months on a regular basis without Licensure (BCO 19-1)?

…makes it clear that one should not be regular pulpit supply without Licensure (BCO 19-1 & 22-5 and 6). He does not fulfill any of the three categories from which pulpit supply is usually drawn (ministers, licentiates, or ruling elders). The BCO is clear…

metadata.synopsis: Antioch Session challenged Peterson’s licensure based on his prior divorce, creation and local-flood views, reversal of a committee recommendation, and close vote; it also challenged his regular preaching before licensure. The SJC rejected the licensure specifications because Presbytery had thoroughly examined repentance and doctrinal adherence, and no definitive PCA standard required exclusion on these facts. It sustained the pre-licensure supply issue under BCO 19-1, 22-5, and 22-6 and enjoined greater future circumspection. The licensure remained undisturbed; the ruling was expressly case-specific.
